title: A Week of Work Vanished After a Rebase
intro: A developer rebased their feature branch, hit conflicts, 'resolved' them in a panic, and force-pushed. Now five commits of their feature are simply gone from the branch.

steps.prompt: Look at the branch's current history.
steps.fake_output:
a9b8c7d (HEAD -> feature/reports) resolve conflicts
9f8e7d6 (origin/main) release v2.4.0
steps.hint: Only one commit left on top of main.

steps.prompt: Check the reflog on the developer's machine for where the branch was before the rebase.
steps.fake_output:
a9b8c7d HEAD@{0}: rebase (finish): returning to refs/heads/feature/reports
...
5e6f7a8 HEAD@{14}: commit: reports: export to CSV
4d5e6f7 HEAD@{15}: commit: reports: date filters
steps.hint: The reflog records where HEAD was before the rebase started.

steps.prompt: Create a rescue branch at the pre-rebase commit so nothing can be lost while you sort things out.
steps.hint: A branch pointing at the old commit keeps all of its history alive.

steps.prompt: Confirm the rescue branch contains all five commits.
steps.fake_output:
5e6f7a8 reports: export to CSV
4d5e6f7 reports: date filters
3c4d5e6 reports: pagination
2b3c4d5 reports: query builder
1a2b3c4 reports: scaffold
9f8e7d6 release v2.4.0
steps.hint: All five feature commits should be visible.

steps.prompt: Restore the remote feature branch from the rescue branch, safely.
steps.hint: --force-with-lease refuses to overwrite if someone else pushed in the meantime.

resolution: During conflict resolution the developer effectively discarded their own commits, then force-pushed that result over the remote. The commits weren't actually deleted — git keeps them in the reflog for about 90 days — so creating a branch at the pre-rebase commit rescued everything in minutes. Two habits prevent the panic entirely: create a backup branch before any big rebase ('git branch backup-before-rebase'), and use 'git push --force-with-lease' instead of '--force', which refuses to overwrite remote work you haven't seen. If a rebase goes wrong partway through, 'git rebase --abort' returns you to exactly where you started.
